answer.evidence: The unit is drawn face-on, like the bookshelf reference. Rows 1-4 are a pale gray band with highlight rows, and the red strip at rows 5-6 follows directly with no front-edge line and no eave shadow. That reads as a front-facing header, not a horizontal top surface, so I count only about 2 rows as a rim. The shelf boards at rows 13-14, 21-22 and 29-30 are 2-row light/gray strips, which is rim-like. The product rows sit in dark navy openings and are seen face-on. The body has no top surface and no receding side face, only a 26-row front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a shelf-style gondola with a red header band, a grey-white frame, and rows of orange and red goods. Measured facts support it: 20 visible tones per tile, matching prop-well-roofed (20) and above prop-stall-cheese (17) and prop-hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines carry a tint (a dark blue-grey beside the frame, a dark red-brown beside the goods) and it does not read as a black sticker line. The frame has about 5 lightness steps and the goods show several tones each. The product rows give it grain and repetition, though by eye it is slightly cleaner and less textured than the stall reference. It would sit acceptably next to the references without looking thinner or flatter.

Rows 5-6 are a red sign strip, which is also vertical. Below that are a dark navy back panel and shelves whose boards show only 2-row front edges (rows 13-14, 21-22, 29-30), which count as rims. The goods are seen straight on and no shelf surface is visible from above. This is a front elevation with no real top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a shelf gondola with a grey-blue frame, a red header strip and three shelves of orange and red packs. The measured facts match the stall and well references: 20 visible tones per tile against 17 and 20, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted rather than black. By eye, the dark blue-grey outline sits next to the frame and the dark red-brown next to the packs, so it reads as dark material tone, not a sticker line. Individual packs carry highlight and shadow dots, and the frame has a light, mid and dark ramp, so there are no large flat areas. The frame and header ramps are slightly shallower (about 4 steps) than the 5-6 on the stall and well, and the texture is moderate rather than rich, but the piece would not look thinner or flatter beside the references.
